t: a branch. A group of threads that hang down from the garment like a branch from a tree.
the corner of the garment. The corner of the garment.
of the same material as the garment. From the material from which the garment is made (as explained below 3:5).
like the tzitzit of the head. The hair of the head.
a number by Torah law. But by rabbinic law it has a number, as explained below, halachah 6.
like the sky. The color of the sky.
and winds it around the branch. Wraps it around the other threads in the branch.
a measure by Torah law. And see below, halachah 6, how it is practiced.
two commandments. Two directives.
"and they shall make for themselves tzitzit". A directive to make the branch of tzitzit.
"and they shall put on the tzitzit of the corner a thread of tekhelet". A directive to wind the tekhelet.
does not prevent. One can fulfill the one commandment without fulfilling the other.
and the white was cut off and reduced up to the corner. The white threads were torn off entirely.
and the four tzitzit prevent one another. Only if he attached tzitzit to all four corners has he fulfilled the commandment.
from the corner. The corner of the garment.
from the knot of the thumb. The distance from the middle joint of the thumb to the tip of the nail.
and doubles them in the middle. So that the four threads hang from both sides of the garment.
and every finger-breadth is by the thumb. A finger-breadth is measured by the width of the thumb (and its measure is explained in Hilchot Sefer Torah 9:9).
and one of the eight threads shall be a thread of tekhelet. That he spins a single thread, part of which is tekhelet and part white (Responsa of Maimonides, 286).
for we ascend in holiness and do not descend. Since he begins with white, he ends with it, so as not to diminish its importance.

so that it be adjacent to the corner of its kind. So that next to the corner of the garment there be a thread of the same kind as the garment and in its color. But most of the windings are from the tekhelet thread.
no fewer than seven and no more than thirteen. Seven corresponds to the seven heavens, and thirteen corresponds to the seven heavens and the six spaces between them (Babylonian Talmud, Menachot 39a).
and the beauty of the tekhelet. The pleasing way of tying the tekhelet.
and he must unravel it until it is like the tzitzit of the hair of the head. He leaves the end of the branch without windings, so that the threads remain separated like the hairs of the head.
one who makes white without tekhelet. For the tekhelet does not prevent, as explained above, halachah 4. For example, one who has no tekhelet (see below 2:9).
twisted. Spun from several fine threads.
is counted only as one thread. Although the thread is twisted from eight separate threads, it is not counted as eight threads but as one.
for the sake of tzitzit. For the purpose of the commandment.
the hairs that are plucked from the animal. Hairs that were torn off and not sheared.

from the remnants of the warp that the weaver leaves at the end of the garment. A garment is made of lengthwise threads (called the warp) and crosswise threads (called the weft). Sometimes after weaving, the fringes of the lengthwise threads remain.
from the shearing. The wool that was sheared for spinning.
the condemned city. A city most of whose inhabitants are idol worshipers, all of whose property must be burned (Hilchot Avodah Zarah 4:6).
from consecrated property. From a sheep or wool belonging to the Temple treasury.
one who bows to an animal, its wool is invalid for tzitzit. Although the wool is not forbidden because of this (see Hilchot Avodah Zarah 8:1), nevertheless one should not use it for a commandment.
for it has changed. When it was worshiped it was wood, and now threads have been made from it (compare Hilchot Issurei Mizbe'ach 3:14).

and tzitzit that was made from what was made previously. That the attaching of the threads was done in a manner that is not effective for fulfilling the commandment of tzitzit, and only after the tzitzit was already tied did he correct the matter, as explained in the following halachot.
a corner that has tzitzit in it. A piece of garment to which tzitzit threads have already been attached.
he attached the threads, etc.. He attached threads to two corners of the same garment and tied each corner properly, and afterward cut the threads so that two valid tzitzit were formed.
intertwined with one another. Joined to one another.
he attached tzitzit on top of tzitzit. He tied tzitzit threads on a corner that already had threads.
if he intended to nullify the first. When he tied the second threads, his intention was to nullify the first threads.
when he added, he invalidated all. For a corner with two branches is invalid because of "do not add."
one who attaches to a garment of three. Corners, which is not obligated in tzitzit, as explained below 3:3.
